title: Learning Self-Correction in Vision–Language Models via Rollout Augmentation
claim: Our method reaches higher accuracy than all baselines at a fraction of their compute cost, breaking the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff.
layout: 1 panel scatter-line plot, accuracy vs time, starred 'ours' in top-left corner
description: A single scatter-and-line plot. The x-axis is rollout generation time per step in seconds (400 to 800) and the y-axis is accuracy in percent (66 to 72). Three baselines (GSPO in light blue-grey, GRPO in dark navy, SRPO in cyan) are each drawn as a line joining a circle (rollout.n=8) to a square (rollout.n=16). The squares sit at higher time and slightly higher accuracy. A dashed grey horizontal line marks the Qwen3-VL-8B-Thinking reference at 70.5. The eye goes first to the large red star in the top-left, labeled 'Octopus-8B' in bold red italic with '71.7'. That point is above every baseline and to the left of all of them. A legend in the top right explains the line colors and marker shapes. The background is light grey and the axes are minimal.
caption: Comparison of accuracy and training efficiency across different RL methods initialized on Qwen3-8B-VL-Instruct. Octopus achieves the best average accuracy across seven benchmarks while requiring substantially less rollout time.
abstract: Self-correction is essential for solving complex reasoning problems in vision-language models (VLMs). However, existing reinforcement learning (RL) methods struggle to learn it, as effective self-correction behaviors emerge only rarely, making learning signals extremely sparse. To address this challenge, we propose correction-specific rollouts (Octopus), an RL rollout augmentation framework that synthesizes dense self-correction examples by recombining existing rollouts. This augmentation simultaneously improves sample efficiency due to rollout reuse and stabilizes RL optimization through balanced supervision. Furthermore, we introduce a response-masking strategy that decouples self-correction from direct reasoning, avoiding signal conflicts and enabling both behaviors to be learned effectively. Building on this, we introduce Octopus-8B, a reasoning VLM with controllable self-correction capability. Across 7 benchmarks, it achieves SoTA performance among open-source VLMs, outperforming the best RLVR baseline by 1.0 score while requiring only $0.72\times$ training time per step.
